- misc: the unit `*JUTest` classes.
`ant testSystem` runs `SystemJUTest` over `ProjectFortress/tests/`, the interpreter's test folder. It runs about 680 tests in four shards, in about 2 to 4 minutes.
`ant testSpecData` runs the specification's 130 extracted examples (`SpecData/examples/basic`, `preliminaries`, `advanced`) under walk, in about a minute. The gate runs it after the two suites.
The newest gate summary has the exact counts and times of the last landed run:
    git log -1 --name-only --format= -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt'
The two suites work in the same way:
- Each suite runs `ant compileAll` first, as every `ant` test target does, so it never tests stale classes. After an edit of Java or Scala, that build empties `default_repository/caches` (`build-and-caches.md`, "Building"). Each analyses or compiles the Fortress code that it tests, in private caches.
- Each JVM gets 768 MB, a 32 MB stack and `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, whatever the shell exports. The run steps of the compiled tests get `JAVA_FLAGS=-Xmx4g -Xss64m`, also whatever the shell exports.
- Each suite deletes `ProjectFortress/test-caches` when it starts. Each JVM keeps its caches in a folder of its own under it, so that the JVMs do not overwrite each other's entries. Temporary files go to `ProjectFortress/test-tmp/`.
- The results are in `ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/fast-<track>/` and `system-<i>/`, as `TEST-<class>.txt`.
To run a suite:
- Run one suite at a time in a tree, because each suite deletes the `test-caches` that the other uses.
- Read the verdict in the line before `Total time:`: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` means zero failures, and `BUILD FAILED` means at least one. Every `ant` test target ends with these lines, and exits non-zero when it failed.
- To compare test counts, compare the sum of the four shards. A file added to `tests/` moves every later file to another shard.
- If a suite's count fell, a `.test` file or a `tests=` line almost always went missing.
## The switches that the harness reads
Put a `-D` switch on the `java` line of a run by hand; the `java` line in `harness-one.sh` is a model. On the `ant` line, it does not reach the suites' JVMs.
- `-Dtests=<dir>`: the folder that `SystemJUTest` runs, in place of `tests/`.
- `-Dfortress.suite.shard=i/n`: run shard i of n only.
- `-Dfortress.unittests.count=N`: run N files at most.
- `-Dfortress.unittests.seed=<value>`: the order of the files. Each run prints its seed as `FORTRESS_UNITTESTS_SEED=...`.
- `FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1` for `SystemJUTest`, `-Dfortress.junit.verbose=true` for the compiled tests' classes: show the output of passing tests too.
- `-Dfortress.junit.reset=false`: `CompilerJUTest` and `LibraryJUTest` keep their caches folder. Without it, they empty it when they start.
## Outside the gate
- `ant testNotPassing` runs the interpreter programs of `ProjectFortress/not_passing_yet/`, which are expected to fail. It fails if one of them passes.
- No suite and no stage of the gate runs the team demos, the programs of `ProjectFortress/demos/`. Keep each of the 52 demos that `DemoTests` lists reaching its end (P-79). Check them with the demo driver below, not with `ant testDemos`, whose test of the output is weaker:
  - If your change edits walk, the parser, a phase that both paths run, a class under `nativeHelpers/` that a `builtinPrimitive` string of the interpreter's library names (`interpreter.md`, "Natives") or the interpreter's library, run the driver once, after your last edit of code.
  - Print the driver with `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-team-demos/REPORT.md#Commands worked out'`. Save the first script that it prints, under "The demo driver", without the text around it, as `tmp/run-demos.sh` in your tree.
  - From the tree's root, after you set up the call, run `bash tmp/run-demos.sh tmp/demos`. It runs long, so run it in the background with a log (`session.md`, "Long commands"). It runs the demos under walk one at a time and writes `tmp/demos/summary.tsv`.
  - The driver's last line of output, before the log's `EXIT=` line, must read 'demos: 52 run, 52 reached their end'. A demo reaches its end if it exits 0 and its output holds no "fail" in upper or lower case.
  - If your change breaks a demo and you know how to repair the demo, repair it in the commit of your change. Otherwise, report the demo, its output and the ledger row that holds the missing feature, as a defect that your change makes or uncovers.
- Nothing runs these folders: `not_working_compiler_tests/`, `not_working_library_tests/`, `not_working_static_tests/`, `obsolete_interpreter_tests/`, `long_term_not_working/`, `linker_tests/`, `compiler_regressions/`. Put every new test in a gated test folder. A test of a defect that fails today is an `XXX` test there (`tests-writing.md`).
## When to run a whole suite
- The gate runs every suite once, on the tree that lands (`gate.md`). Your brief says whether you run the gate.
- If your edit changes the Java or Scala of the checker, of walk, of a phase that both paths share or of such a class under `nativeHelpers/`, run all the tests that it reaches. Run them once, after your last edit of code. The run needs no commit.
  - For the checker, run `ant testQuick`: the compiler, othercompiler and library tracks at once (below).
  - For walk, run `ant testSystem`. It is the same as its four shards run by hand.
  - For a shared phase (under `compiler/`: name binding, DSL grammars, desugaring, the marking of overloaded calls in `OverloadRewriter`), the parser or such a class, run both.
- Quote the verdict lines and the command in your report, with the commit if your code is committed.
- If the gate later runs on a tree that holds other changes too, that tree is another code state. Your run and the gate's run do not repeat each other.
- After an edit of the code generator (`codegen/`, `OverloadSet`) or the run time (`runtimeSystem/`), run your own tests, and the four-thread atomic runs (`gate.md`) if `compiler.md` asks for them. Leave the whole tracks to the gate.
- After every other change, run only your own tests, through the scripts below, and the demos where "Outside the gate" asks for them. Leave the rest to the gate. This includes an edit of either library, though it reaches many tests.
The suites do not check these:
- the bytecode optimizer, which nothing in the compiler calls;
- DSL grammars, except one program whose phases the misc track runs: `syntax_abstraction_tests/ForUse.fss`;
- the linker's aliasing of apis;
- `fortress unparse`;
- the round trip of the `.tfi` and `.tfs` caches;
- a behaviour above one thread that one run of each suite at four threads does not hit.
If your edit is in one of these, your own tests are its only check. Say so in your report.
## One test, or a few
Each script and `fortress junit` below ends with the verdict of JUnit's text runner: `OK (n tests)`, or `FAILURES!!!` with the counts. Read the verdict there: the exit code is 0 whatever the verdict.
### Interpreter tests
Run interpreter tests (`ProjectFortress/tests/`) from the tree's root, after you set up the call:
    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh <tree>/tmp/h1 \
        ProjectFortress/tests/X.fss [ProjectFortress/tests/X.test] [more files ...]
- It runs `SystemJUTest` with testSystem's JVM settings, at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, on a folder that holds only the files that you name.
- It keeps its cache in the folder `<scratch-dir>.cache`. It starts from that cache while the build and the library sources are those that filled it. Otherwise, or with `COLD_CACHE=1`, it starts empty. Its first line says `cache filled` or `cache empty`.
- It runs the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/` and builds nothing. After you edit Java, Scala or a parser grammar, run `ant compileAll` first. If your tree has no build, seed it or build it as `worktrees.md` says.
- Give it a scratch directory that holds nothing else. The script deletes the directory when it starts and when it ends.
- If a test has an `X.test` file (its keys for a refusal at load), name it beside its `X.fss`.
- It takes 15 to 25 s with an empty cache, mostly to analyse the library, and about 4 s with a filled one. Name several files in one call to run them in one JVM.
- It shows the output of passing tests too, and removes the Java stack frames.
To see the whole diagnostic, with its Java stack, run the program directly, from `ProjectFortress/` as the harness does, because an import is looked up in the current directory first:
    cd ProjectFortress && ../bin/fortress -debug stacktrace tests/X.fss
The direct run and the harness use different heaps (`interpreter.md`, "Running a program").
### Compiled tests
Compiled tests are the `.test` files in `compiler_tests/`, `library_tests/` and `other_compiler_tests/`. They link with the library's jars in the tree's `default_repository/caches`. If a build started the caches again, or the tree's caches are empty, run the library order first (`build-and-caches.md`).
The script is `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh`. `climb-batch-N` is the folder's real name, not a placeholder. Run your own tree's copy: it runs the tree that it is in.
    ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh <label> \
        ProjectFortress/compiler_tests X.test Y.test > <tree>/tmp/junit-<label>.txt 2>&1
- `<label>` is any word. It marks the run's lines in the output. The script writes to standard output only, so redirect it to your `tmp/`.
- With `ONE_JVM=1`, the whole list runs in one `fortress junit` run, in one JVM. The compile and link tests run before the run tests, as in the suite. Without `ONE_JVM=1`, each file gets its own JVM.
- It removes the named components' entries from the tree's `default_repository/caches` before the whole list and after it, not between files. So a link test and the run test that uses its jar pass in one call, with or without `ONE_JVM=1`.
- It runs the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/` and builds nothing, as `harness-one.sh` does.
- It removes the Java stack frames, and cuts each line at 240 characters.
- Its JVMs keep their temporary files in the tree's `tmp/`, and run at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`.
To run the same list in one JVM without the script, and without its removal of cache entries:
    cd ProjectFortress && ../bin/fortress junit compiler_tests/X.test compiler_tests/Y.test
Run all the new files of one test folder together, in one JVM, as the suite does. A test that passes alone can fail beside others.

To run one unit-test class: `ant testOnly -DtestPattern=BitsJUTest`. It uses the tree's own caches and the shell's `FORTRESS_THREADS`.
To run tracks of testFast whole, run their target. Each target runs its tracks as testFast does, with the same JVMs and private caches:
- `ant testCompiler`: the compiler and othercompiler tracks.
- `ant testOtherCompiler`: the othercompiler track.
- `ant testLibrary`: the library track.
- `ant testQuick`: the three tracks.
# The base build, seeded worktrees and the old code
**seeding**
: Making a worktree with a copy of the build and caches of a built, clean worktree. `seed-worktree.sh` makes the copy and rewrites the paths in it (`SKILL.md`, "The caches").
**base build**
: Clean worktree at the base, built in place by ant, or seeded. Every other worktree is seeded from it.
**old code**
: Base's code, run from the base build with a private caches folder.
Once the base build is built, run its code only as "Running the old code" says, with a private caches folder outside it. Any other run writes into the caches that every worktree is seeded from.
## Finding or building a base build
- If your brief names a base build, use it.
- If not, look in `git worktree list`. Earlier base builds are at paths such as `/home/user/fortress-base<N>`. A worktree can be your base build if it passes three checks:
  - `git -C <it> rev-parse HEAD` prints your base;
  - `git -C <it> status --porcelain` prints nothing;
  - it holds `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`.
- If no worktree passes them, build one at a path of your own, outside the main tree. It takes about 200 s: start the build and the library order detached, with the `nohup` line of `session.md`, "Long commands". `<base-commit>` is your base: the commit that your brief names, else your tree's `HEAD` when you start. Say so in your report.
      git worktree add --detach <base-build> <base-commit>
      cd <base-build>          # then set up the call as build-and-caches.md says
      ant compileAll
      # then the library order (build-and-caches.md), then this walk run, which warms walk's caches:
      bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss
      git status --porcelain   # must print nothing: the seeding script refuses a base build that is not clean
If you check a fix against its old code, use a base build at the commit that the fix starts from. If a brief names the fix's base, the fix starts there. If not, the fix starts from `git merge-base <its branch> main`, or from the parent of its first commit on `main`.
## Seeding a worktree
A build, and a run of `bin/fortress` without a private caches folder, walk's too, write into the caches of the tree that they run in. So build and run only in a tree whose caches no other agent uses. Your brief says where you work. If your work builds or runs code and your brief gives you no tree of your own, seed a worktree of your own instead of building one. Then work only there.
Seeding takes about 3 s and 206 MB of disk. The new worktree runs walk and the compiled path right away, with the library already compiled.
    explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh <base-build> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]
- The script checks out `<branch>`: a local branch, else origin's, else a new branch cut from `<start-point>`, by default the base build's commit. With `-`, it makes a detached worktree at `<start-point>`.
- If the script exits 2, the base build is not built or not clean, and the script made nothing. Then make the worktree with `git worktree add`, build it yourself, and say so in your report.
- If the worktree already exists, the script keeps its branch. If it already has a build, the script keeps that too. `SEED_FORCE=1` replaces it.
- If you start in a worktree that has no build, seed it in place: name it as `<new-worktree>`, and its branch as `<branch>`.
- The script lists the library sources that differ from the base build's commit. Before a compiled run, take for each the step that `build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library", gives.
- If the script warns that the copied build is the base's, run `ant compileAll`, then the library order. Without the warning, `ant compileAll` keeps the seeded caches.
- If another agent seeded your worktree, make the script's two lists yourself: `git diff --name-only <base> -- Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin` for the library sources, and `git diff --name-only <base> -- ProjectFortress/src ProjectFortress/astgen build.xml` for the warning.
- Reuse another tree's build or caches only through this script.
## Running the old code
If your worktree holds an edit and you need the base's behaviour, run the old code instead of reverting your edit. For example, see a test fail, or compare a program's old and new output.
`old-fortress.sh` runs the base build's `bin/fortress`. It sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the base build and `FORTRESS_CACHES` to the private caches folder that you name, over your settings. Name a folder inside your worktree's `tmp/`:
    OLD=explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches compile P.fss     # the compiled path ...

    sizeField:ZZ32 = first.size + second.size
    depthField:ZZ32 = 1 + (first.depth MAX second.depth)
    getter size():ZZ32 = sizeField
    getter depth():ZZ32 = depthField

    getter asFlatString():String =
        typecase (first.asFlatString, second.asFlatString) of

(* Under walk, a builtinPrimitive body whose string names a static helper of nativeHelpers runs that helper, its arguments and result carried at the declared types. *)
component NativeHelperBindingWalk
export Executable

less(a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT")
plus(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleDoubleArith.doubleAdd")
ladd(a:ZZ64, b:ZZ64):ZZ64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleLongArith.longOverflowingAdd")
both(a:Boolean, b:Boolean):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleBoolean.booleanAnd")
cat(a:String, b:String):String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeConcatenate")
len(a:String):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen")
wide(a:ZZ64):ZZ = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.makeZZfromZZ64")
nn(a:ZZ32):NN32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleUnsignedIntArith.makeNN32FromZZ32WithSpecialCompilerHackForNN32ResultType")
ch(a:ZZ32):Char = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleChar.charMakeCharacterWithSpecialCompilerHackForCharacterResultType")
code(c:Char):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleChar.charCodePointWithSpecialCompilerHackForCharacterArgumentType")
upper(c:Char):Char = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleChar.charToUpperCase")
bazS(s:String):String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")
bazI(n:ZZ32):String = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")

run():() = do
  assert(less(1, 2), true, "less(1, 2)")
  assert(less(3, 2), false, "less(3, 2)")
  assert(plus(2.5, 3.0), 5.5, "plus(2.5, 3.0)")
  x: ZZ64 = 4000000000
  assert(ladd(x, x), 8000000000, "ladd")
  assert(both(true, false), false, "both")
  assert(cat("ab", "cd"), "abcd", "cat")
  assert(len("abcde"), 5, "len")
  assert(wide(x) wide(x), 16000000000000000000, "wide")
  assert(nn(7), unsigned(7), "nn(7)")
  assert(ch(65), 'A', "ch(65)")
  assert(code('a'), 97, "code('a')")
  assert(upper('q'), 'Q', "upper('q')")
  assert(bazS("x"), "baz x", "bazS")
  assert(bazI(7), "baz 7", "bazI")
end

end

## 5. The measurements, before and after

All runs: `nproc` 4, OpenJDK 25.0.4.1. The harness runs at four threads; direct runs at one. Each harness run started with an empty cache.

### 5.1 The 25 gating tests

| Code state | Verdict |
|---|---|
| S0 | `OK (25 tests)` (09:20:09 UTC) |
| S1 | `Tests run: 25,  Failures: 20,  Errors: 0` (09:21:53 UTC) |
| S2 | `OK (25 tests)` (09:29:07 UTC) |
| S3 | `OK (25 tests)` (09:27:49 UTC) |

On S1 every program stops at load on the library's own binding, which is what item 340 predicts:

    com.sun.fortress.exceptions.InterpreterBug: Library/FlatString.fss:35:5-36:89:
    Native helper com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen: no Java type carries FlatString, the type of self.

- **The five tests that pass on S1** are refusal tests whose key the library's refusal also satisfies, or whose own refusal comes first: `NativeHelperMisspeltWalk`, `NativeHelperMisfitWalk`, `NativeHelperUncarriedWalk`, `NativeHelperUncarriedSelfFunctionalWalk` and `NativeHelperUncarriedSelfFlatStringWalk`.
- **The other four refusal tests fail on S1** with "Refused at load, but did not satisfy load_exception_contains".

On S3:

    . interpret tmp/h-s3/tests/NativeHelperCarriedSelfFlatStringWalk
    FlatString sizes: 0 5 5 40
     OK (time = 561ms)
    . interpret tmp/h-s3/tests/NativeHelperUncarriedSelfFlatStringWalk
     OK Saw expected refusal at load

### 5.2 My own programs

| Program | S0 | S1 | S2 | S3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OwnFlatStringSize | refused at load: "… no Java type carries FlatString, the type of self.", rc=1 | refused by the library's binding, rc=1 | refused by its own binding, rc=1 | refused by its own binding (`OwnFlatStringSize.fss:6:3-103`), rc=1 |
| OwnFlatStringParam | `before`, `10`, rc=0 | refused by the library's binding | `before`, `10`, rc=0 | `before`, `10`, rc=0 |
| OwnJavaStringParam | `before`, `10`, rc=0 (via `old-fortress.sh`) | not run | `before`, `10`, rc=0 | `before`, `10`, rc=0 |
| name clash | `NullPointerException`, rc=1 | same | same | same |
| api claim | "Failed to find overload member \|\| for _RewriteFnOverloadDecl at …/Library/String.fss:579.35", rc=1 | same | same | same |

The two ways for a program to pass way 1's check both stop the run before any closure loads:
- **A component named `FlatString`** takes the library component's name in the linker. The library's `String` then finds no api `FlatString` to import. The message is "Cannot invoke "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.env.APIWrapper.getTopLevelRewriteNames()" because "api_cw" is null", at `Driver.java:315`.
- **A program that claims api `FlatString`** replaces the library's component. The library's `String` then fails on the program's object, which has no `||`.

A program that replaced the component completely, natives and all, would be a copy of the library's file. Any run can already put such a copy in its current directory.

### 5.3 A shadowing copy of the library's file

On S3, the new test run from `tmp/probe/shadowdir/`, which holds a copy of `Library/FlatString.fss`, printed `FlatString sizes: 0 5 5 40` with rc=0. Way 1 holds wherever the file is read from. Way 2 would have refused this run.

### 5.4 The wider runs

The skill asks for both of these after an edit of walk's Java and of the library (`references/tests-running.md`). Both ran on S3.

    BUILD SUCCESSFUL / Total time: 4 minutes 10 seconds

That is 724 tests: climb batch 24's gate's 723 (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-24/gate/summary.txt`) plus the new test.

    bash tmp/run-demos.sh tmp/demos      (the driver of rung-team-demos/REPORT.md, "Commands worked out")
    demos: 52 run, 52 reached their end

**Not run:**
- The compiled tracks, which the shadow does not reach.
- The distance stage, the only stage that checks a binding of the component `FlatString` against its helper. By reading, the F-298 rewrite makes the moved binding `nativeStrlen(self)` with `self` a `FlatString`, which extends `String`, so it should type. This is not measured.

### 5.5 The diagnostic

The diagnostic was a temporary print in `javaForSelf(FType)`, active under `-Dfortress.probe340=true`, in a build of its own. It was removed before S2, S3 and the wider runs.

    probe340 declarer=FlatString way1.component=OwnFlatStringSize way2.file=…/tmp/probe/OwnFlatStringSize.fss way5.FortressLibraryBinds=null way4.apiViaLibrary=noapi way4.apiViaOwnEnv=noapi env=BetterEnvLevelZero top=true … topLevel.at=Component:OwnFlatStringSize sameTop=true

## 6. The defects met

1. **A parameter declared at a program's own `FlatString` or `JavaString` is carried by its name.**
   - Mechanism: `javaFor` carries a parameter's declared type by its name (`StaticNativeApp.java:54`). `unbox` takes `v.getString()` (`:231`), which `FObject.getString` answers with the type's name (`FObject.java:33-35`).
   - Effect: `slen(x: FlatString)` answers 10 on S0, S2 and S3. It is row 847's symptom on a parameter instead of `self`.
   - Not repaired by the shadow. Way 1 could repair it by resolving the parameter's declared type in the declaration's environment; that cost is not measured.
   - Home: 3, or 2 if the curator reads the printed `builtinPrimitive` comment ("the one whose Java parameter and result types carry the declared types", `FortressBuiltin.fsi:19`) as settling it.
   - Row (passes `ledger.py check --rows` except for its `?` number):

       | ? | under walk, a `builtinPrimitive` helper binding with a parameter declared at a program's own type named `FlatString` or `JavaString` loads, and its call passes the type's name: `slen(x: FlatString): ZZ32` bound to `simpleConcatenate.nativeStrlen`, beside `object FlatString end`, answers 10 | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (walk) | `Specification/library/default-libraries.tex`, "FortressBuiltin" | none | probe of review-queue item 340 | siblings: 847, 846. `StaticNativeApp.javaFor` carries a parameter's declared type by its name, `FlatString` and `JavaString` in `String` (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:54`, at dc571c1f3); `unbox` takes `v.getString()` (`:231`), which `FObject.getString` answers with the type's name (`interpreter/evaluator/values/FObject.java:33-35`). Probe in `explorations/perf-probes/loader-declaring-type/REPORT.md`, section 4: prints 'before', '10', rc=0, on the base and on the shadow; the same with `object JavaString`. Fix: read the parameter's type by its declaration, as the probe's way 1 reads `self`'s. |

2. **A program whose component has a library component's name stops with a `NullPointerException`.**
   - The specification forbids two components with one name. Walk gives no refusal that names the clash; it crashes at `Driver.java:315`.
   - This is the clash that keeps way 1 sound, but its message names nothing.
   - Home: 2 or 3.
   - Row (passes the check except for its `?` number):

       | ? | under walk, a program whose component has the name of a library component, as `component FlatString export Executable`, stops with a `NullPointerException` in the linker, not with a refusal that names the clash | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (walk) | `Specification/basic/components/apis.tex`, "Component and API Identity" | none | probe of review-queue item 340 | "Every component has a unique name, used for the purposes of component linking" and "A fortress does not allow the installation of distinct components with the same name." `commandLineComponent` gives the program's wrapper the name (`interpreter/Driver.java:495`, at dc571c1f3), so `ensureApiImplemented` returns it for the library's import of api `FlatString` (`:436-437`), and `injectTraitMembersForDesugaring` finds no exported api of that name (`:315`): 'Cannot invoke "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.env.APIWrapper.getTopLevelRewriteNames()" because "api_cw" is null', rc=1. Probe: the report `explorations/perf-probes/loader-declaring-type/REPORT.md`, section 4. Workaround: another name. |

3. **`NativeHelperUncarriedSelfFlatStringWalk`'s key is the exact text of the library's own refusal.**
   - So on S1 the test passed although the refusal was the library's.
   - It is sound on S0 and S3, where the library's binding loads.
   - It is a weakness of the test, so no row. A batch that moves the binding could name, in that test, a helper that no library binding uses, such as `nativeConcatenate`.

4. **Way 5 does not see the library's type at load.** This is not a defect of the tree, since the tree does not use that lookup.

The shadow itself showed no defect.

## 7. Decisions

1. **Way 1 built** (section 3). The closest alternative is way 4. It could be added to way 1 as a second condition, at the cost of its three dependences.
2. **`JavaString` stays refused by its name.** Walk's library has no declaration of that name.
3. **The binding moved is `size`, onto `nativeStrlen`.** The alternatives, and what each would need:
   - `|self|` onto the same helper;
   - `cmp` onto `stringOps.compareTo`;
   - `flatConcat` onto `simpleConcatenate.nativeConcatenate`;
   - `javaSubstr` onto `stringOps.substring`. Its `Useful.substring` clamps bounds where the glue class's `String.substring` throws (`useful/Useful.java:974-982`; `glue/prim/FlatString.java:152-157`), so that move changes the value of an out-of-range call.
4. **The top level of the environment, not the environment itself, gives the component** (the trap in section 2).
5. **One new gated test in the patch.** The existing refusal test is unchanged.
6. **The `native` flag is not checked.** The component's name suffices by the linker's rule.
7. **The distance stage is not run.**

- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4503-4507`: "…which it reads by the type's name, for the types of \library\ whose names no program can give its own types." This would stay true but become incomplete.
- `StaticNativeApp.java:81-86`, the comment of `javaForSelf`, which the shadow rewrites.

#!/bin/bash
# harness-one.sh <scratch-dir> <file.fss>... : rung C's harness-one.sh (explorations/compile-ladder/
# rung-interp-coercion/, itself rung I's shape): the testSystem harness (SystemJUTest, the class build.xml's
# testSystem shards run) over a directory holding only the named test files, with the JVM settings of
# build.xml's systemShard macro and a private cache. Run from FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh.
#
# The scratch directory is deleted when the call starts and when it ends. The private cache is the folder
# <scratch-dir>.cache beside it, kept between calls. A call starts from what that folder holds when it was
# filled under the implementation now built (ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp, which ant compileAll
# writes) and from the Fortress sources now on the source path outside the scratch directory (the .fss and
# .fsi files of Library, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin, ProjectFortress/test_library and ProjectFortress);
# otherwise it empties the folder first. COLD_CACHE=1 empties it in any case. The folder is stamped only when
# the JVM ends normally, so a call that is killed leaves it to be emptied by the next one.
set -u
S=$(realpath -m -- "${1:?scratch dir}") ; shift
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:?}
C=$S.cache
BUILT=$FH/ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp

(* Under walk, getEnvironment, getProperty and the three thread prints read the characters of a rope made by ||, a SubString and EmptyString, and match those of flat strings. *)
component NativeHelperStringRopeWalk
import String.{CatString, SubString, EmptyString}
import System.{getEnvironment, getProperty}
export Executable

isSubString(s: String): Boolean = typecase s of
    SubString => true
    else => false
  end

run():() = do
  long: String = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" || "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
  assert(|long|, 52, "|long|")
  assert(long.depth, 1, "the concatenation is a rope")
  unset: String = "FORTRESS_NO_SUCH_VARIABLE_OR_PROPERTY"

  (* a name that is set, flat, as a rope and as a SubString *)
  pathFlat = getEnvironment("PATH", "?")
  assert(pathFlat =/= "?", true, "PATH is set")
  pathRope: String = CatString("PA", "TH")
  pathSub: String = CatString("xPA", "THx")[1#4]
  assert(isSubString(pathSub), true, "pathSub is a SubString")
  assert(getEnvironment(pathRope, "?"), pathFlat, "getEnvironment at a rope name")
  assert(getEnvironment(pathSub, "?"), pathFlat, "getEnvironment at a SubString name")
  assert(getEnvironment(unset, long), long.asFlatString, "getEnvironment at a rope default")
  assert(getEnvironment(unset, pathSub), "PATH", "getEnvironment at a SubString default")
  assert(getEnvironment(unset, EmptyString), "", "getEnvironment at an EmptyString default")
  assert(getEnvironment(EmptyString, "?"), "?", "getEnvironment at an EmptyString name")

  versionFlat = getProperty("java.version", "?")
  assert(versionFlat =/= "?", true, "java.version is set")
  versionRope: String = CatString("java.", "version")
  versionSub: String = CatString("xjava.", "versionx")[1#12]
  assert(isSubString(versionSub), true, "versionSub is a SubString")
  assert(getProperty(versionRope, "?"), versionFlat, "getProperty at a rope name")
  assert(getProperty(versionSub, "?"), versionFlat, "getProperty at a SubString name")
  assert(getProperty(unset, long), long.asFlatString, "getProperty at a rope default")
  assert(getProperty(unset, versionSub), "java.version", "getProperty at a SubString default")
  assert(getProperty(unset, EmptyString), "", "getProperty at an EmptyString default")
  assert(getProperty(EmptyString, "?"), "?", "getProperty at an EmptyString name")

  assert(match("a.c", "abc"), true, "match")
  assert(match("a.c", "abd"), false, "match not")
  assert(match("", ""), true, "match of the empty strings")

  printThreadInfo(long)
  printThreadInfo(pathSub)
  printThreadInfo(EmptyString)
  printWithThread(long)
  println()
  printWithThread(pathSub)
  println()
  printWithThread(EmptyString)
  println()
  printlnWithThread(long)
  printlnWithThread(pathSub)
  printlnWithThread(EmptyString)
end

end
EOF

(* Under walk, the library's FlatString answers its natives, and the operations built on them, at flat strings, the empty one among them, with self carried as a Java String. *)
component NativeHelperCarriedSelfFlatStringWalk
import FlatString.{...}
export Executable

run():() = do
  e = ""
  w = "hello"
  long = ("a"^20 || "b"^20).asFlatString
  assert(e.size, 0, "the empty flat string's size")
  assert(w.size, 5, "a five-character flat string's size")
  assert(|e|, 0, "the empty flat string's |self|")
  assert(|w|, 5, "a five-character flat string's |self|")
  assert(long.size, 40, "the flat form of a forty-character concatenation has size 40")
  assert(w.javaSubstr(1).size, 4, "javaSubstr(lo) reads self.size")
  assert((w || "!").size, 6, "a flat concatenation's size")
  assert("été".size, 3, "a string with accented characters counts its Java chars")

  assert("a\"b\\c".asExprString, "\"a\\\"b\\\\c\"", "asExprString quotes and escapes")
  assert(e.asExprString, "\"\"", "asExprString of the empty string")

  assert(w.get(0), 'h', "get(0)")
  assert(w.get(4), 'o', "get(4)")

  assert(w.cmp(w), 0, "cmp of equal strings")
  assert("abc".cmp("abd"), -1, "cmp below")
  assert("b".cmp("a"), 1, "cmp above")
  assert("a".cmp("abc"), -2, "cmp of a prefix")
  assert(e.cmp(w), -5, "cmp of the empty string")

  assert("ABC".cicmp("abc"), 0, "cicmp of strings equal but for case")
  assert("ABC".cicmp("abd"), -1, "cicmp below")
  assert("b".cicmp("A"), 1, "cicmp above")
  assert(e.cicmp(e), 0, "cicmp of the empty strings")

  assert(w.javaSubstr(1, 3), "el", "javaSubstr(1, 3)")
  assert(w.javaSubstr(0, 5), "hello", "javaSubstr of the whole")
  assert(w.javaSubstr(2, 2), "", "javaSubstr of an empty range")
  assert(e.javaSubstr(0, 0), "", "javaSubstr of the empty string")

  assert(w.javaIndexOf('l'), 2, "javaIndexOf found")
  assert(w.javaIndexOf('h'), 0, "javaIndexOf at the start")
  assert(w.javaIndexOf('z'), -1, "javaIndexOf not found")
  assert(e.javaIndexOf('a'), -1, "javaIndexOf in the empty string")
  assert("aΣb".javaIndexOf('Σ'), 1, "javaIndexOf past U+00FF")

  assert(flatConcat("ab", "cd"), "abcd", "flatConcat")
  assert(flatConcat(e, w), "hello", "flatConcat of the empty string")
  assert(flatConcat(e, e), "", "flatConcat of two empty strings")

  assert("abc".javaRegExpMatches("a.c"), true, "javaRegExpMatches")
  assert("abc".javaRegExpMatches("b"), false, "javaRegExpMatches of a part")
  assert(e.javaRegExpMatches(""), true, "javaRegExpMatches of the empty string")
  assert("a,b,c".javaRegExpSplit(",", 0), "a", "javaRegExpSplit, the first piece")
  assert("a,b,c".javaRegExpSplit(",", 2), "c", "javaRegExpSplit, the last piece")
  assert("a,b,c".javaRegExpSplit(",", 3), "", "javaRegExpSplit past the last piece")
  assert(e.javaRegExpSplit(",", 0), "", "javaRegExpSplit of the empty string")

  assert(w.uncheckedSubstring(1#3), "ell", "uncheckedSubstring")
  assert(w.indexOf('l').holds, true, "indexOf found")
  assert(w.indexOf('l').get, 2, "indexOf's index")
  assert(w.indexOf('z').holds, false, "indexOf not found")
  assert("abc" < "abd", true, "<")
  assert("abd" < "abc", false, "< not")
  assert(("ABC" CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP "abc") = EqualTo, true, "CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP equal")
  assert(("abc" CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP "ABD") = LessThan, true, "CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP below")
  assert("ab" || "cd", "abcd", "||")
  assert(e || e, "", "|| of the empty strings")
  println("FlatString sizes: " e.size " " w.size " " |w| " " long.size)
end

end
EOF

content.content:
# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The last ref keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

# Rung T, climb batch 26: the string family onto helpers (items 310 and 340; row 846)

- problem: 161 of the one library's 449 live native bindings name walk's glue classes, which the compiled path cannot run (F-32), the string family's 20 among them; the five over `String` read a rope's type name (row 846; `explorations/reviews/string-natives-2026-11-05.md`, section 2.3), and `FlatString`'s methods could not name a helper, since walk carried no `self` for a type named `FlatString` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:88` at 4d27fbcc5)
- spec: none; `grep -rn builtinPrimitive Specification --include=*.tex` prints only `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`; the library chapter only includes the api `FortressBuiltin` (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:37-39`)
- precedent: the team's pair of a native over `FlatString` beside an overload over `String`, `Library/Writer.fss:33-35`, `:45-49`, `Library/File.fss:20-22`; the flattening `typecase` of `Library/FlatString.fss:137-140` and `Library/String.fss:84-87`; the loader's way 1 of `explorations/perf-probes/loader-declaring-type/shadow.patch:1-145`
- deviation: FlatString's line separator binds `stringOps.lineSeparator` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/stringOps.java:72`), not a helper of `systemOps` as the record's fork 22 placed it, since the checker cannot read `systemOps` against the interpreter's prelude (NEW-T-1); the loader's refusal of a helper parameter declared `String` (`StaticNativeApp.java:70`) is beyond the probe's patch; the comment of `javaForSelf(String)` is worded anew (`StaticNativeApp.java:96-102`)
- historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/stringOps.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simplePrintln.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/systemOps.java, Library/FlatString.fss, Library/FortressLibrary.fss, Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, Library/System.fss, Library/System.fsi

## What changed and why

Commits on `wip/rung-string-natives`: `15d81c1c1` (the tests, before the change), `19e9dbda5` (the change), `8b6fca9b5` (the line separator onto `stringOps`).

- **Walk's loader.** `NativeApp.java:201` passes `StaticNativeApp.find` the declaring type, not its name. `find(String, Applicable, FType)` (`StaticNativeApp.java:163`) reads `self`'s carrier through the new `javaForSelf(FType)` (`:122`): the object `FlatString` that the component `FlatString` declares at its top level, told by `declaringComponent` (`:136`) from the top level of the type's environment, carries `self` in a Java `String`; every other type is read by its name by `javaForSelf(String)` (`:103`), unchanged, so a program's own type named `FlatString` or `JavaString` still carries none. This is the probe's Java, hunk for hunk; the comment of `javaForSelf(String)` is reworded to say what the code does.
- **The last step, taken.** The new `javaForParameter` (`StaticNativeApp.java:70`) carries a parameter's declared type as `javaFor` does, except `String`: the loader refuses a helper parameter declared `String` at load, 'no Java type carries the declared type of parameter a.' (`:178-180`). A parameter declared `FlatString` or `JavaString`, and a result declared `String`, are still carried in a Java `String`.
- **`FlatString`'s methods**, 11 of 13 (`Library/FlatString.fss:35-101`), name helpers; `=` and `flatConcat(self, b:Char)` stay on `FlatString$Eq` and `FlatString$Concat` (item 331). `natLineSeparator` (`:25-26`) and `match` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4615`) name helpers.
- **The five over `String` as pairs.** `printThreadInfo`, `printWithThread`, `printlnWithThread` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4628-4644`, api `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2633-2639`) and `getEnvironment`, `getProperty` (`Library/System.fss:41-56`, api `Library/System.fsi:34-41`, with `import FlatString.{FlatString}` at `System.fss:14` and `System.fsi:14`) are each a public native over `FlatString` whose body is exactly `builtinPrimitive("...")`, beside an overload over `String` that flattens in the library's `typecase` and stops with `fail` in its `String` arm. `printThreadInfo(a:Number)` stays on `StringPrim$PrintThreadInfo`.
- **Helpers.** New, public and static, no state: in `stringOps.java` `asExprString` (`:44`, quoting through `Unprinter.enQuote` as `FString.toString` does, `interpreter/evaluator/values/FString.java:31-33`), `compareToIgnoreCase` (`:48`), `javaSubstr` (`:53`, Java's `substring`, which raises out of range), `javaRegExpMatches` (`:57`), `javaRegExpSplit` (`:62`), `match` (`:67`), `lineSeparator` (`:72`); in `simplePrintln.java` `printThreadInfo`, `printWithThread`, `printlnWithThread` (`:40-50`), each the glue's text (`StringPrim.java:64-81`); in `systemOps.java` `getEnvironment` (`:24-27`). No existing method changed; no new class.

Each helper's name is the only method of that name in its class, so the compiled rewrite adds its `Char` transfer helpers to `get` and `javaIndexOf` (`compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:186-188`).

- `StaticNativeApp`: the imports, `FLAT_STRING_COMPONENT`, `javaForSelf(FType)`, `declaringComponent`, `find(String, Applicable, FType)` and its message `declarer.getName()`, as the patch. ## What changed and why

Commits on `wip/rung-string-natives`: `15d81c1c1` (the tests, before the change), `19e9dbda5` (the change), `8b6fca9b5` (the line separator onto `stringOps`).

- **Walk's loader.** `NativeApp.java:201` passes `StaticNativeApp.find` the declaring type, not its name. `find(String, Applicable, FType)` (`StaticNativeApp.java:163`) reads `self`'s carrier through the new `javaForSelf(FType)` (`:122`): the object `FlatString` that the component `FlatString` declares at its top level, told by `declaringComponent` (`:136`) from the top level of the type's environment, carries `self` in a Java `String`; every other type is read by its name by `javaForSelf(String)` (`:103`), unchanged, so a program's own type named `FlatString` or `JavaString` still carries none. This is the probe's Java, hunk for hunk; the comment of `javaForSelf(String)` is reworded to say what the code does.
- **The last step, taken.** The new `javaForParameter` (`StaticNativeApp.java:70`) carries a parameter's declared type as `javaFor` does, except `String`: the loader refuses a helper parameter declared `String` at load, 'no Java type carries the declared type of parameter a.' (`:178-180`). A parameter declared `FlatString` or `JavaString`, and a result declared `String`, are still carried in a Java `String`.
- **`FlatString`'s methods**, 11 of 13 (`Library/FlatString.fss:35-101`), name helpers; `=` and `flatConcat(self, b:Char)` stay on `FlatString$Eq` and `FlatString$Concat` (item 331). `natLineSeparator` (`:25-26`) and `match` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4615`) name helpers.
- **The five over `String` as pairs.** `printThreadInfo`, `printWithThread`, `printlnWithThread` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4628-4644`, api `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2633-2639`) and `getEnvironment`, `getProperty` (`Library/System.fss:41-56`, api `Library/System.fsi:34-41`, with `import FlatString.{FlatString}` at `System.fss:14` and `System.fsi:14`) are each a public native over `FlatString` whose body is exactly `builtinPrimitive("...")`, beside an overload over `String` that flattens in the library's `typecase` and stops with `fail` in its `String` arm. `printThreadInfo(a:Number)` stays on `StringPrim$PrintThreadInfo`.
- **Helpers.** New, public and static, no state: in `stringOps.java` `asExprString` (`:44`, quoting through `Unprinter.enQuote` as `FString.toString` does, `interpreter/evaluator/values/FString.java:31-33`), `compareToIgnoreCase` (`:48`), `javaSubstr` (`:53`, Java's `substring`, which raises out of range), `javaRegExpMatches` (`:57`), `javaRegExpSplit` (`:62`), `match` (`:67`), `lineSeparator` (`:72`); in `simplePrintln.java` `printThreadInfo`, `printWithThread`, `printlnWithThread` (`:40-50`), each the glue's text (`StringPrim.java:64-81`); in `systemOps.java` `getEnvironment` (`:24-27`). No existing method changed; no new class.

# Rung T, climb batch 26: the string family onto helpers (items 310 and 340; row 846)

- problem: 161 of the one library's 449 live native bindings name walk's glue classes, which the compiled path cannot run (F-32), the string family's 20 among them; the five over `String` read a rope's type name (row 846; `explorations/reviews/string-natives-2026-11-05.md`, section 2.3), and `FlatString`'s methods could not name a helper, since walk carried no `self` for a type named `FlatString` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:88` at 4d27fbcc5)
- spec: none; `grep -rn builtinPrimitive Specification --include=*.tex` prints only `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`; the library chapter only includes the api `FortressBuiltin` (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:37-39`)
- precedent: the team's pair of a native over `FlatString` beside an overload over `String`, `Library/Writer.fss:33-35`, `:45-49`, `Library/File.fss:20-22`; the flattening `typecase` of `Library/FlatString.fss:137-140` and `Library/String.fss:84-87`; the loader's way 1 of `explorations/perf-probes/loader-declaring-type/shadow.patch:1-145`
- deviation: FlatString's line separator binds `stringOps.lineSeparator` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/stringOps.java:72`), not a helper of `systemOps` as the record's fork 22 placed it, since the checker cannot read `systemOps` against the interpreter's prelude (NEW-T-1); the loader's refusal of a helper parameter declared `String` (`StaticNativeApp.java:70`) is beyond the probe's patch; the comment of `javaForSelf(String)` is worded anew (`StaticNativeApp.java:96-102`)
- historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/stringOps.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simplePrintln.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/systemOps.java, Library/FlatString.fss, Library/FortressLibrary.fss, Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, Library/System.fss, Library/System.fsi

## What changed and why

Commits on `wip/rung-string-natives`: `15d81c1c1` (the tests, before the change), `19e9dbda5` (the change), `8b6fca9b5` (the line separator onto `stringOps`).

- **Walk's loader.** `NativeApp.java:201` passes `StaticNativeApp.find` the declaring type, not its name. `find(String, Applicable, FType)` (`StaticNativeApp.java:163`) reads `self`'s carrier through the new `javaForSelf(FType)` (`:122`): the object `FlatString` that the component `FlatString` declares at its top level, told by `declaringComponent` (`:136`) from the top level of the type's environment, carries `self` in a Java `String`; every other type is read by its name by `javaForSelf(String)` (`:103`), unchanged, so a program's own type named `FlatString` or `JavaString` still carries none. This is the probe's Java, hunk for hunk; the comment of `javaForSelf(String)` is reworded to say what the code does.
- **The last step, taken.** The new `javaForParameter` (`StaticNativeApp.java:70`) carries a parameter's declared type as `javaFor` does, except `String`: the loader refuses a helper parameter declared `String` at load, 'no Java type carries the declared type of parameter a.' (`:178-180`). A parameter declared `FlatString` or `JavaString`, and a result declared `String`, are still carried in a Java `String`.
- **`FlatString`'s methods**, 11 of 13 (`Library/FlatString.fss:35-101`), name helpers; `=` and `flatConcat(self, b:Char)` stay on `FlatString$Eq` and `FlatString$Concat` (item 331). `natLineSeparator` (`:25-26`) and `match` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4615`) name helpers.
- **The five over `String` as pairs.** `printThreadInfo`, `printWithThread`, `printlnWithThread` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4628-4644`, api `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2633-2639`) and `getEnvironment`, `getProperty` (`Library/System.fss:41-56`, api `Library/System.fsi:34-41`, with `import FlatString.{FlatString}` at `System.fss:14` and `System.fsi:14`) are each a public native over `FlatString` whose body is exactly `builtinPrimitive("...")`, beside an overload over `String` that flattens in the library's `typecase` and stops with `fail` in its `String` arm. `printThreadInfo(a:Number)` stays on `StringPrim$PrintThreadInfo`.
- **Helpers.** New, public and static, no state: in `stringOps.java` `asExprString` (`:44`, quoting through `Unprinter.enQuote` as `FString.toString` does, `interpreter/evaluator/values/FString.java:31-33`), `compareToIgnoreCase` (`:48`), `javaSubstr` (`:53`, Java's `substring`, which raises out of range), `javaRegExpMatches` (`:57`), `javaRegExpSplit` (`:62`), `match` (`:67`), `lineSeparator` (`:72`); in `simplePrintln.java` `printThreadInfo`, `printWithThread`, `printlnWithThread` (`:40-50`), each the glue's text (`StringPrim.java:64-81`); in `systemOps.java` `getEnvironment` (`:24-27`). No existing method changed; no new class.

- `StaticNativeApp`: the imports, `FLAT_STRING_COMPONENT`, `javaForSelf(FType)`, `declaringComponent`, `find(String, Applicable, FType)` and its message `declarer.getName()`, as the patch. - **The five over `String` at a string that is not flat**: the characters, where the base passed the type's name (`CatString`, `SubString`, `EmptyString`), above.

- The loader: climb batch 25's carrier of `self` by the declaring type's name, and the probe's way 1 (`explorations/perf-probes/loader-declaring-type/REPORT.md`, section 3).
- Ways the language and the library offer for item 310 (the strings review, section 6): (a) the loader flattens every string argument; (b) the pairs, taken; a private native beside a public overload (item 332's form), not taken. For item 340: way 1, taken; ways 2 to 8 of the probe, not taken.
